knowledge_point.title: Determining Whether Two Lines in Standard Form are Perpendicular

question.:question/problem: Which of the following lines is perpendicular to $x+5y=10?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
For the two lines to be perpendicular, their slopes must multiply to $-1.$

To find the slope of the given line $x+5y=10,$ we convert to slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+5y & =10 \\ 5y & =-x+10 \\ y & =-\frac{1}{5}x+2\end{aligned}
$$

In slope-intercept form, the slope is the $x$-coefficient. So, the slope of the given line is $-\frac{1}{5}.$

Looking at the answer choices, the line $y=5x-4$ has a slope of $5.$

Multiplying the slopes together, we have

$$
(-\frac{1}{5})\cdot 5=-1.
$$

Since the slopes multiply to $-1,$ we conclude that the line $y=5x-4$ is perpendicular to the given line.

\begin{aligned}12x-4y & =5 \\ -4y & =-12x+5 \\ y & =3x-\frac{5}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

In slope-intercept form, the slope is the $x$-coefficient. So, the slope of the given line is $3.$

Looking at the answer choices, the line $y=-\frac{1}{3}x+3$ has a slope of $-\frac{1}{3}.$

Multiplying the slopes together, we have

$$
3\cdot (-\frac{1}{3})=-1.
$$

Since the slopes multiply to $-1,$ we conclude that the line $y=-\frac{1}{3}x+3$ is perpendicular to the given line.
